The '''Bimms''' were diminutive [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Mammal/Legends|mammalians]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bimmisaari/Legends|Bimmisaari]]. A floppy-eared, furred [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] species, the Bimms had a reputation as a peaceful, hospitable people. Sharing their homeworld with a [[Near-Human]] species also known as the [[Bimm/Legends|Bimm]], the two species were completely unrelated biologically but shared a [[Bimmini/Legends|language]] and cultural identity as Bimms. Many descriptions of Bimm culture and society ignored the biological differences between the two species. Not all Bimms hewed to their people's stereotypical, inoffensive demeanor, however; the [[Sith acolyte/Legends|Sith Acolyte]] and serial murderer [[Toki Tollivar]] rose to power in the wake of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], causing problems for the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] until his death during the early years of the [[Mandalorian Wars]].

==Biology and appearance==
Having evolved on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bimmisaari/Legends|Bimmisaari]], the furry Bimms were slightly taller than the [[Near-Human]] [[Bimm/Legends|Bimms]], with an adult height of 1.0 to 1.6 [[Meter/Legends|meters]], with the [[Gender/Legends|females]] being slightly taller on average. They were covered in short fur that ranged from black to tan in [[Color/Legends|color]]. Their faces had floppy [[Ear/Legends|ears]], long muzzles, and small black [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. Their [[Limb/Legends|hands]] possessed three long fingers and a thumb each.<ref name="AA" />

Both species called themselves simply "Bimms" and lived harmoniously with each other in their shared forest [[City/Legends|cities]]. They considered themselves to be a united people, and were considered as such by the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. [[Marriage/Legends|Intermarriage]] between the two Bimm species was not uncommon, though genetic incompatibilities required such couples to adopt if they wanted children.<ref name="AA" />

==Society and culture==
[[File:Bimmisaari.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Bimms rushing to greet the ''Millennium Falcon'' during the Galactic Civil War]]

Though the Bimm species had lived together for almost all of their recorded history, certain aspects of their culture were more associated with one species than with another. While some sources attributed these cultural tendencies to one species or the other,<ref name="AA" /> sources such as [[Mammon Hoole]] presented them as aspects of a single, shared culture.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>

The language [[Bimmini/Legends|Bimmini]], which was used by both species, was sung, rather than spoken.<ref name="AA" /> A Bimm conversation had a seemingly mystical quality, sounding to Human ears like songs being sung in five-part harmony.<ref name="HTTES">''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> Bimms were particularly good [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]], and felt the day was incomplete without a good round of shopping and haggling. The art of bargaining was respected in their culture, and fair dealing was highly honored. However, cheating and theft were tantamount to murder in their society. Bimms were also noted for their yellow clothing.<ref name="AA" />

Both species were noted for their mild-tempered, peaceful tendencies, which was the reason the two species lived together in harmony. This tendency extended to non-Bimm visitors from offworld, who would be treated as honored guests.<ref name="AA" /> The Bimm greeting ritual involved a reception line which each visitor would walk through. In complete silence, each Bimm in line would reach out and gently touch the visitor's head, arm, or back. More important visitors would attract correspondingly large crowds in the procession.<ref name="HTTE" /> This honor did not extend to armed visitors, however, who would be expected to leave their weapons behind.<ref name="HTTES" />

==History==
[[File:Toki.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Sith Acolyte Toki Tollivar]]
Evolving on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bimmisaari/Legends|Bimmisaari]], the Bimms first made contact with the [[galactic community]] during the [[Great Manifest Period/Legends|Great Manifest Period]] with the colonization of their world by a [[Near-Human]] [[Bimm/Legends|species]]. Growing together as a united society the two species became known collectively as the Bimm and were well respected playwrights and experts in hospitality. During the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], forces from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] moved along the [[Lesser Lantillian Route/Legends|Lesser Lantillian Route]], upon which the Bimm homeworld was located, to mount a counteroffensive to the [[Sith Empire (Exar Kun)/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

By the time of the [[New Sith Wars]], the Republic had grown significantly weaker from centuries of war, leaving the Bimm homeworld within the territory controlled by the [[Hutt Empire|Hutt regime]] and a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] faction called the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]]. The Bimm remained under Hutt control long after the destruction of the Brotherhood, remaining in space contested by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="TEA" /> Having quietly withdrawn from the corrupt Republic decades before the war, the Bimms found that their world was remote enough that few took notice of them, allowing their people to escape most of the chaos of the Republic's fall and the later oppression of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="HTTES" /> During the [[Sy Myrthian Insurrection]], the Bimm were conquered by the Empire and the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] driven off the world.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the Bimms remained neutral, but friendly toward the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and later, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="AA" /> While controlled by the [[Greater Maldrood]] as of [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the Bimm were conquered by [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]].<ref name="TEA" /> Around this time, a delegation from the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] traveled to meet with the Bimm, hoping to convince them to join their fledgling government.<ref name="HTTE" /> The [[Shi'ido]] [[Sentientologist|anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] included an entry on the Bimms in his publication ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> A major trade center, the Bimm were decimated in [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]] by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] during their [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invasion]] of the galaxy. By the end of the war, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] made a push to free the Bimm, saving what was left of their homeworld and species from total annihilation.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="The New Jedi Order Sourcebook">''[[The New Jedi Order Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==Bimms in the galaxy==
[[File:Toki_Tollivar.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Tollivar, a.k.a. Kelven Garnatrope, also known as the Corellian Strangler]]
While content with remaining on their homeworld, those Bimms who went offworld were usually traders or business people. Some Bimms became adventurers, whether as scoundrels who somehow worked their way into the circles of nobility, or as artists who followed heroes in order to witness great deeds which they could record in ballads. Entire communities of Bimms were also found in enclaves off Bimmisaari, which were noted for their hospitality.<ref name="AA" />

[[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]] of the species were inclined to join the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], as [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were highly revered in Bimm society for their heroism and monastic lifestyle. Although most joined the Jedi, at least one furred Bimm, [[Toki Tollivar]], defected to the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] and became an [[Sith acolyte/Legends|adept]] and learned to wield a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. At the end of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] Tollivar began a private campaign of revenge and serial murder, before being killed by the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Demagol]] posing as [[Rohlan Dyre]].<ref name="KOTOR38">[[Knights of the Old Republic 38|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 38]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The name "Bimm" first appeared in [[Timothy Zahn]]'s [[1991]] novel, ''[[Heir to the Empire]]''. [[1993]]'s ''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]'', a supplement for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' written by [[Bill Slavicsek]], described the Bimm species in more detail, and provided illustrations. While both Heir to the Empire and Heir to the Empire Sourcebook describe the Bimms as "half-furred", an illustration by [[Allen Nunis]] and [[Paul Daly]] included in Heir to the Empire Sourcebook made them appear to be simply short Humans.

In [[1995]], a [[Star Wars: Heir to the Empire (comic series)|comic book adaptation of ''Heir to the Empire'']] was published by [[Dark Horse Comics]]. The adaptation's artwork by [[Olivier Vatine]] and [[Fred Blanchard]] depicted clearly non-Human aliens with large floppy ears. The same year, however, the [[Premiere Limited]] set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]], published by [[Decipher]], included a card identifying a character from the original film as [[Rycar Ryjerd/Legends|Rycar Ryjerd]], a Bimm smuggler. Ryjerd, having been portrayed by actor [[Marcus Powell]] without extensive prosthetic makeup, resembled the Human-like Bimms from West End Games illustrations more closely than the floppy-eared aliens drawn by Vatine and Blanchard. In [[1998]], a card in the [[Jabba's Palace Limited]] expansion set identified another background character in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], again played by an actor without extensive makeup, as Rycar Ryjerd's son Rayc.

The confusion was resolved in 1998 by [[Daniel Wallace]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''. The Bimmisaari entry included a drawing of two floppy-eared Bimms, but noted that the planet was also inhabited by a small Human-like species with the same name. Later works, such as [[2001]]'s [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']] by [[Ann Margaret Lewis (real person)|Ann Margaret Lewis]] and various [[Wizards of the Coast]] supplements for their ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'', went into more detail about the history and shared culture of the two Bimm species.
